subject: physics

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2020 (Q8) and March 2024 (Q7) — Section A, 2 marks each time. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced from those papers. Physics hand-checked: heat is the energy transferred between two bodies because of a temperature difference and is measured in joule; temperature is the degree of hotness, measured in kelvin, and it decides the direction of the transfer.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Heat
lines: Heat is the energy that passes from one
body to another because of a difference of
Its SI unit is the joule.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Define heat as transferred energy and give the joule.
steps.why: Heat is not stored in a body. It is the energy crossing the boundary between two bodies, and once it has crossed it becomes internal energy of the receiving body.
common_mistakes: Saying a hot body contains more heat. A body contains internal energy; heat is only what is transferred.

recall.must_convey: That heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference and is measured in joule.

steps.memory_tip: Heat is energy that is being transferred, and it is measured in joule.

steps.label: Temperature
lines: Temperature is the degree of hotness of a
body. Its SI unit is the kelvin.

lines.text: Temperature sets the heat flow direction

lines: Heat passes from the body at the higher
temperature to the one at the lower
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give the kelvin and the direction of flow.
steps.why: Two bodies at the same temperature exchange no net heat however large they are, so it is the temperature and not the quantity of energy that sets the direction.
common_mistakes: Treating heat and temperature as the same quantity. A large cold body can hold more internal energy than a small hot one.

recall.must_convey: That temperature is the degree of hotness, measured in kelvin, and it decides which way heat flows.

steps.memory_tip: Temperature in kelvin, heat in joule. Temperature sets which way the heat goes.

insider_note: Two marks means two contrasts — what each quantity is, and its unit. A pair of definitions written with no units usually loses one mark.
